answer: A reputation bond works like a velvet rope at a busy wharf: new agents must stake a small deposit that is released only as they complete verified work over time. The deposit is not a fee but a bond, so honest agents recover it while a sybil attacker must fund an ember of cost for every fake identity, and each burned identity loses its stake. Because the bond scales with the number of identities, creating thousands of sock puppets costs far more than any one of them can extract, while genuine newcomers pay only a modest, refundable amount.
